summary: Unusual spike in IdP-signed JWT usage across multiple internal accounts
description:
Issue summary:
We observed an anomalous spike in authentication events where IdP-issued JWTs (SAML->OIDC pipeline) were used to exchange for short-lived service tokens. These exchanges originated from a small set of IPs that are not common for our workforce and targeted multiple internal service and user accounts.

Impact:
- Potential credential or token re-use affecting 3 internal accounts and multiple service tokens issued to CI/CD runners.
- No evidence yet of data exfiltration, but some high-privilege service tokens were minted and used to call internal admin APIs.
- Could affect deployment pipelines and onboarding workflows if tokens are revoked without a coordinated mitigation.

Environment:
- Production SSO (IdP: corporate Okta) federated to Redwood SSO proxy in us-east-1.
- Time window: 2026-03-12 03:12:00 UTC -> 2026-03-12 03:45:00 UTC.

Observed indicators / logs:
- Auth audit logs show ~180 token exchanges with IdP-signed JWTs in the 33-minute window.
- Source IPs: 34.120.12.87, 34.120.13.192 (ASN / cloud provider observed).
- User agents: headless-bot/1.2, python-requests/2.31.0 (some variance).
- Several exchanges returned service tokens with admin-scoped claims for infra-ops account.
- No immediate 5xx or runtime errors observed on admin APIs; however, token usage patterns were unusual (burst requests to /v1/admin/keys).

Steps to reproduce (for validation):
1) Query auth audit index: query by event_type:token_exchange AND source_ip in [34.120.12.87,34.120.13.192] AND timestamp between 2026-03-12T03:00:00Z and 2026-03-12T04:00:00Z.
2) Correlate returned token IDs with internal token-usage logs in service-audit index.
3) Verify Okta org logs for suspicious OAuth/OIDC grant activity for the same time window.

Initial mitigation actions taken:
- Rotated affected service keys for svc-data-ingest and infra-ops.
- Forced SSO session revocations for implicated human accounts (alice@redwood.com).
- Throttled token exchange endpoint for non-corp IP ranges and added temporary WAF rule to block the two IPs.
- Opened an incident bridge and notified Legal and Product Security.
- Created this internal-support ticket to capture investigation and follow-up remediation tasks.
investigation_notes: 03/12 03:20 UTC - Alert from auth-monitoring: token_exchange_rate > 25/min for SSO proxy; triggered oncall.
03/12 03:25 UTC - Confirmed 180 exchanges from two external IPs; fetched raw auth logs and correlated to service-audit.
03/12 03:28 UTC - Hypothesis A: credentials/token capture from phishing or compromised CI/CD runner. Hypothesis B: misconfigured third-party integration replaying JWTs.

03/12 03:34 UTC - Checked Okta sign-in logs: no interactive human sign-in from these IPs, but several token-grant events via service app client. Opened ticket with Okta support for additional metadata.
03/12 03:40 UTC - Identified a CI runner artifact that had environment variable containing long-lived client assertion; rotated that credential and invalidated prior tokens.
03/13 09:00 UTC - SRE ran forensics on the two IPs: both map to ephemeral cloud VMs; abuse reports filed with provider.
03/14 10:30 UTC - Security team requested expanded audit retention for token_exchange logs and started payload-level parsing to extract JWT ids for replay detection.
comments: Aisha Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-12: Initial detection and mitigation steps listed. On-call will coordinate rotations.
Diego Morales (Assignee) 2026-03-12: Applied WAF block for observed IPs and forced session revocations for implicated users. Continuing log correlation.
Priya Shah (Product Security) 2026-03-12: Requesting Okta export of app-level grant logs and list of affected app client IDs; also advise rotating any CI client assertions.

Samir Gupta (SRE) 2026-03-13: Found a Jenkins runner in project 'release-automation' with a stale service assertion. Rotated and removed hard-coded token from job config. Investigating whether token was exfiltrated via job artifacts.
Legal 2026-03-13: Please collect timeline for any external communications; we'll prepare a notice template if customer-facing impact is discovered.
Diego Morales 2026-03-14: Filing for a post-incident review once we confirm no further exchange spikes. Recommend making token-exchange rate limit permanent for non-corp ranges.
next_steps: Complete full token lineage mapping for all exchanged tokens during window and mark any sessions/tokens for permanent revocation where appropriate.
Coordinate with Identity team and Okta support to determine the exact grant flow used and whether the client application was configured with overly-broad scopes.
Implement a permanent rule in API gateway to restrict token_exchange endpoint to corp IP ranges and known CI egress ranges, with an allowlist for validated third-party integrators.
Schedule a postmortem (blameless) with SRE, Product Security, and Build/CI owners. Link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/INT-130001-Postmortem
Assess whether additional EDR/forensics on implicated developer workstations is warranted based on CI findings.
resolution: Partial mitigation complete: affected credentials rotated, WAF blocks applied, Okta support engaged. Full root cause pending confirmation of whether token values were exfiltrated from a CI artifact or replayed by a third-party integration. Postmortem scheduled. No customer data confirmed accessed at time of last update.
notes_for_followup: Revisit rate-limiting thresholds for token_exchange endpoint as a platform configuration item for Q2 roadmap.
Add automated alert for abnormal ratio of token_exchange events to interactive sign-ins for any given account.
Ensure CI templates do not accept raw client assertions and add linting check in internal-tools repo.
